title: Normalized Word Frequencies
description: Count words in text without regard to capitalization. A word may contain ASCII letters or digits, with one apostrophe inside it (for example, `can't`). Ignore punctuation and return a dictionary mapping normalized words to counts.

solution.explanation: A regular expression extracts words and contractions, then casefold normalizes capitalization. Counting the tokens in a dictionary combines words that differ only by case. Punctuation and whitespace do not become tokens.

tests.hint: No tokens produce an empty mapping.
Case variants count as the same word.
An apostrophe inside a token stays with the word.
The pattern permits a single internal apostrophe.
Repeated whitespace does not create empty words.

args: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
tests.hint: Count each normalized occurrence in a sentence.
Only ASCII letters are included by this specification.
